newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi urges prudence over Jan PSBR.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi urges prudence over Jan PSBR.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Saturday that a positive public sector deficit for January would not influence the Italian government's decision on whether to have a mini-budget.
State auditor Andrea Monorchio was quoted earlier as saying Italy's public sector borrowing requirement in January should be some three trillion lire, compared to 12.35 trillion lire in January 1996.

Ciampi, speaking to reporters before attending a conference held by the Aspen Institute in Rome where he was due to speak, confirmed the government was expecting "very positive figures" when January's PSBR is announced on Monday.
But he warned that fundamental changes in 1996, including to taxes on mineral oils and pension payments, meant "one must be very prudent in making comparisons with last year".

Asked whether a positive deficit in January would provide the government with any indications as to the amount and timing of an eventual mini-budget, Ciampi said: "One figure is not enough...The sight of a sparrow doesn't mean it's spring." -- Rome newsroom +396 678 2501
